questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was important for me that i could choose certain courses. Charles University provide a wide range of courses, which made it easy to finds subsitutes. As Charles Univeristy is a 4EU+ partner also made it an "easier" destination. Prague is also famous and fantastic city which was also crucial for my decision. Futher Czech Republic is also a country with a low cost of living, meaning that as a student your money goes a long way, which enables students to participate and get a lot of experiences outside of the university as well.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was easy. The International Office at my faculty was very helpful, and provided a lot of information both before and after my arrival.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Unfortunately due to covid our introduction day was cancelled. However there was an online introduction day instead which provided us with a lot of information and we could then afterwards go to the office for extra information and questions. And I got really fast replies by email, which was nice.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Semi easy. You get the cheaper apartmant if you are in good time. And also everyone is Prauge are looking for roomates so also be sure to look at facebook sites and so.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: The transportation is really good in the city, so it doesn't matter if you don't live near center.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I think that the proces with getting signatures from both universities and sending it back and forth by email was a struggle. Why not have a common digital platform where this takes place.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: E-mail.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: At Charles Univeristy the lecture schedule is published very late, which meant that i WASN'T ABLE TO TAKE ANY of the courses i had pre-approved. This only gave me extras stress that i had to get additional course approved and that all the work done earlier was wasted. Further many of the courses i had pre-approved was even removed....

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't put too much work into your pre-approved courses. It is most likely that you will have to find many new ones when they publish the lecture schedules.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was high in some courses and low i othes. But this was also because i had to change my courses so much and ended up also having a first-year course.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: A hybrid-form and a recording  was avaibale in all my classes which was nice. There as less problem solving which i think it too bad because this is where i really learn the material.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
History of Economic Thought
Principles of Economics II
Economics of Global Business
Introductory Banking
Czech as a Foreign Language I

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Principles of Economics II was a nice macro economics course if you need this. 
Economics of Global Business gave a different view on international business, organization and prolbems realted to multi-national-enterprises

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I didn't encounter any unexpected costs. Everything is extremely affordable in Prague.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Everything from food, transport, cinemas and experiences were all very cheap compared to Denmark.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Due to Covid there was not much available in the start. However later i the semster there was more than evough of social activites. From dinner activities, trips to other cities, pub crawls and so on. So much that you definitely can't participate in everything at all.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: There a lots of great bars and clubs and restaurant. Also the pub run and pub quizzes organized by vollunteer local erasmus people are always funny.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Make sure to take the day trips to other cities. Also there is direct train to many big cities such as Vienna, Budapest and Berlin for weekentrips.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was easy. Expect less kindness from waitors and so. This is not because they are rude, but just the culture.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Make sure to go to all the social activities you can in the beginning to make friends from the first day.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Don't know.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: They have a lot of dogs which is nice. Also everyone drinks beer (almost every day), so that is how many socialize in Prauge.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Pariticpate in social acitivites from day one.
Be open minded as there are meny different people in Prague
Remember to go on trips in the weekend, with the ISIC card you can get as a student at Charles University transportation is s cheap.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Get the student monthly traport card in the app.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: All the new people I met. Definitely.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The Czech people are not very good at english. As an example you have to register at the Foreign Police if you live off-campus. So it is always a good idea to have google translate ready.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
